candidate.name: intraday_return_amount_cross_spectral_phase_lead_59f
candidate.economic_hypothesis: When transaction-amount innovations systematically lead favorable signed price discovery across the complete within-half frequency support, liquidity arrival is more likely information-led than a lagging reaction and may persist from the next open through the third close.
candidate.exact_formula: For each 120-bar half separately, form 119 adjacent log-close returns r_t and destination-bar activity x_t=log1p(amount_{t+1}); demean both length-119 vectors. With the unnormalized DFT convention Z_k=sum_{t=0}^{118} z_t*exp(-2*pi*i*k*t/119), use all positive frequencies k=1..59. Let N=-sum_k Im(conj(X_k)*R_k), D=sum_k abs(X_k)*abs(R_k), and half_score=N/D when D>0. The stock-day score is the arithmetic mean of the morning and afternoon half scores.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_amount_lead_return_correlation_238p
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both use signed within-half close returns and transaction amount with temporal order.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: The terminal factor is one fixed one-step Pearson coefficient between earlier log amount and the next return. Campaign146 uses the antisymmetric phase of the full two-series paths over all 59 positive frequencies, normalizes cross-spectral magnitude rather than covariance, and contains no selected time lag.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_volatility_activity_lead_lag_asymmetry_236p
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both distinguish activity-leading from price-leading behavior.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: The terminal factor contrasts two lag-one Pearson correlations and discards return sign through absolute returns. Campaign146 retains signed returns and measures full-path multiscale phase orientation without a one-lag difference.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_return_amount_cumulative_path_signed_area_238p
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both retain order and orientation in signed return and amount paths.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: Campaign145 integrates normalized cumulative level paths in the time domain and requires positive amount mass and absolute-return closure. Campaign146 demeans log-amount levels and signed returns, discards the zero-frequency level, and aggregates normalized Fourier phase over all positive frequencies. Either statistic can be zero while the other is nonzero.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_amount_price_discovery_alignment_js_238p
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both compare transaction amount with close-return-derived information.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: The terminal JSD factor is simultaneous, unsigned, and order-insensitive after endpoint alignment. Campaign146 retains return sign and the temporal phase relation and cannot be reconstructed from the two marginal distributions.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_amount_conditioned_directional_persistence_spread_236p
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both use activity and signed return dynamics.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: Campaign116 uses a strict all-day median split and adjacent return-sign persistence with 30 observations per group. Campaign146 has no activity threshold, group split, sign-pair state, or support selection and uses all continuous activity magnitudes and signed returns.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_return_spectral_entropy_59f
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both use the same 59 positive Fourier frequencies within each half.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: The terminal factor is an unsigned univariate distribution of return power. Campaign146 is a signed bivariate cross-spectrum; holding return power fixed while shifting the amount path changes Campaign146 but cannot change return spectral entropy.

nearest_complete_definition_review.name: intraday_cumulative_vwap_crossing_rate_240m_candidate49
nearest_complete_definition_review.overlap: Both use close and amount-derived intraday state.
nearest_complete_definition_review.distinction: Candidate49 requires volume to form causal cumulative VWAP and counts reference crossings. Campaign146 reads no volume, forms no VWAP or crossing, remains historical-research-only, and cannot enter either Candidate49 ledger.
